video_title: The AI Bubble Is Deflating. How Low Can Bitcoin Go?
gist: Ryan Sean Adams and David Hoffman frame Bitcoin's new 2026 low (~$55k) as a normal, longer-but-shallower crypto bear market tied to an AI-stock deflation that looks like 2022 rather than 2000 or 2008, driven by slowing Frontier Lab revenue growth, heavy IPO issuance, rate hikes, open-weight model competition and mounting AI credit stress. They flag rumors that AI labs may be weakening classical cryptography (Riemann hypothesis proof, P vs NP, RSA) as crypto's new existential wall of worry, and cover Rune Christensen's $77M Sky margin loan, Venice's revenue doubling, and DeFi tokens on Fidelity.

themes.theme: Bitcoin's new low and bottom calls

insights.claim: Bitcoin set a new 2026 bear-market low of $54,900, breaking below the June low of roughly $57,000-$58,000, after a rally toward $90,000 had led many to expect an unusually mild bear market.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: The failed June bottom invalidates the 'easy bear market' thesis and suggests a longer grind before a durable bottom.

insights.claim: Galaxy's Alex Thorn retracted his October call that the Bitcoin bear market ended in June once price broke below $58,000, now describing the bear as late in time but early in depth.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: A prominent on-chain bull capitulating on his bottom call is a sentiment marker; the market may still have more downside depth even if the cycle is mature in duration.
insights.quote: it's late by the clock, early by the depth

insights.claim: Ben Cowen argues that in prior bear markets Bitcoin bottomed below its realized price, which currently sits around $53,000, implying a plausible bottom under $53k.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: Realized price (~$53k) is a key level to watch; a break below it would be consistent with historical cycle bottoms rather than a signal of breakdown.

insights.claim: Arthur Hayes expects Bitcoin to retest $55k and advises waiting to buy at higher prices with conviction once a government/Fed/Treasury bailout responds to an AI-stock sell-off, executing a 'sell the AI top, buy the crypto bottom' trade.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: Suggests a trigger-based entry: wait for confirmed stimulus/intervention rather than bottom-picking; the first half of Hayes's trade appears to be playing out.
insights.quote: Resist the urge to try and pick the bottom, buy it higher with more conviction once the bailout begins.

insights.claim: Several analysts see historic value: Charlie Edwards cites the long-term holder inflation rate at its most undervalued since November 2022, Raoul Pal says Bitcoin is deep in the buy zone, and Michael Nadeau calls sub-$55k, below the 200-week moving average, deep value territory.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: No one is calling a bottom, but a consensus of cycle analysts frames current levels as an averaging-in zone for long-term positions.

insights.claim: Bitcoin is on eight consecutive red weekly candles; the record is nine, which has only happened once before.
insights.speaker: host (Bankless)
insights.so_what: Near-record streak of no relief bounces signals extreme seller persistence and potential exhaustion.

insights.claim: Downside scenarios: Michael Nadeau says $45k would be a 60-65% drawdown in line with past cycles, while matching 2022's 77% drawdown would imply about $29k; the hosts view sub-$50k as possible but not their base case.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: Frames tail downside levels ($45k, $29k) for risk sizing in case the bear proves as deep as prior cycles.

insights.claim: Crypto will not recover until the debasement trade returns; that trade has been off all year, with gold down 38% from its January high as the AI trade dominated flows.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: Watch gold as a leading indicator: a gold recovery would signal the debasement trade (and crypto) turning back on.
insights.quote: crypto will not come back until the debasement trade is back on

insights.claim: Per Lynn Alden's point, Bitcoin bottomed versus gold at the start of the Iran war: one Bitcoin bought 12 oz of gold then and now buys about 17.5 oz.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: BTC/gold has been rising even as both fall in dollar terms, suggesting relative strength for Bitcoin within the debasement complex.

insights.claim: Michael Howell's global liquidity cycle model (rebound, calm, speculation, turbulence) placed markets entering the turbulence phase, which lasts roughly six to nine months, implying a liquidity-driven turnaround in the first half of 2027 that crypto and gold could follow.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: During turbulence favor cash and bond duration; position for risk assets when liquidity turns up in H1 2027.

insights.claim: The current crypto bear is about 415 days old, longer than 2018 (364 days, -84%) and 2022 (about a year, -77%), but shallower so far at -56%.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: Duration is already above prior cycles while depth is not, so either time or price still has to 'pay' — base case is a normal, grinding bear.

insights.claim: This cycle has fewer 'sins to pay' than prior ones (no FTX or Three Arrows-style collapse; the worst excess was Michael Saylor's leveraged Bitcoin buying), which may explain the shallower drawdown even if timing drags on.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Lower systemic leverage argues against an 80%+ crash, though it does not shorten the bear's duration.

insights.claim: Stablecoin market cap fell about $17 billion (roughly 6% of supply) in 30 days, a rapid contraction not seen before, which the hosts see as the most alarming metric since stablecoins are the liquid capital pool closest to Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Stablecoin supply is a proximate crypto liquidity gauge; a reversal back to growth would be an early bottoming signal.

insights.claim: November 2026 is the worst month on record for Bitcoin ETF flows, with nearly $5 billion of outflows, roughly 5% of ETF holdings dumped in a single month.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Record ETF redemptions show the TradFi holder base is now a source of selling pressure; watch for flows to stabilize.
insights.quote: November is the worst month of Bitcoin ETFs on record.

insights.claim: Bitcoin has fallen about 35% from $86,000 in step with QQQ, but over the last two weeks AI stocks (Nvidia, Intel, semiconductor ETFs, QQQ) made new lows while Bitcoin held above its June lows, showing relative resilience.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Bitcoin decoupling from tech to the downside could signal sellers are exhausted in crypto before equities.

insights.claim: Each crypto bear requires climbing an existential wall of worry; in 2022 it was Gary Gensler and US regulation, and in 2026 it is AI potentially breaking cryptography, which the hosts treat as a tail risk rather than a base case.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: Resolution of the AI-cryptography fear (e.g., credible protocol upgrades) could be the catalyst that ends the bear.

insights.claim: The Nasdaq is down about 20% and turned negative for 2026 amid extreme fear, and Anthropic traded as low as $74, about 10% below its $83 IPO price, for the first time.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: A flagship AI IPO breaking issue price is a classic late-cycle sentiment marker for the AI trade.

insights.claim: Even Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO produced only a one-day relief rally (QQQ circuit-broke to the upside) that was fully erased, indicating the AI sell-off is structural rather than about leadership.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Failed good-news rallies suggest deeper demand/credit concerns; don't buy AI dips on headline catalysts alone.

insights.claim: Revenue growth at Frontier Labs has slowed from roughly 20% month-over-month for three years to an actual decline, and SemiAnalysis cut its 2028 AI accelerator capex forecast by 28%.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Since Frontier Lab revenue sits at the top of the AI pyramid, slowing growth propagates to capex, chips, and AI credit.

insights.claim: Massive equity issuance — SpaceX and Anthropic IPOs, Dario Amodei selling tens of millions in stock, plus pending OpenAI and neocloud IPOs — is overwhelming market demand, echoing Ray Dalio's warning about AI private capital supply in late 2026-2027.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Supply overhang from AI IPOs and lockup expiries can pressure AI equities regardless of fundamentals; watch the OpenAI IPO pipeline.

insights.claim: A rate-hiking cycle is underway with a December hike near 100% priced and another expected in January, while October inflation hit 3.8% (second highest since 2023), lagged oil-price effects are still coming, and new tariffs were announced November 25.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Tightening into high valuations mirrors 2022 and is a headwind for long-duration tech and crypto.

insights.claim: Open-weight models are becoming very good while costing more than 90% less than frontier models, threatening the durable revenues that underpin the AI industry's growth.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Price compression from open models challenges frontier-lab valuations and the downstream capex built on their revenue projections.
insights.quote: Open weight models are getting also very good and they are more than 90% cheaper than the the Frontier models.

insights.claim: Everything in the AI stack — revenues, expectations, loans, and credit — flows downstream of OpenAI and Anthropic token demand, so softening demand forces the entire stack to soften.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: Track frontier-lab token demand as the master variable for AI equities and AI credit.

insights.claim: Ed Zitron argued on CNBC that Anthropic's IPO may mark the end of the AI trade, questioned how OpenAI can go public after raising at a $1.25 trillion private valuation, cited an SEC investigation into Nvidia, and alleged heavy circular financing.
insights.speaker: Ed Zitron (clip)
insights.so_what: Perma-bears getting mainstream airtime signals capitulating sentiment; the circular-financing critique targets Nvidia specifically.
insights.quote: I think that company is horrendously dependent on circular financing to a scale we don't yet know.

insights.claim: The Federal Reserve's November 13 financial stability report found 87% of surveyed market contacts named AI as a top financial stability risk, up 50% from spring, with compute-related debt above $680 billion through October (5x 2023) and guarantees plus unstarted leases potentially topping $3 trillion.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: AI capex is increasingly debt-financed, raising the risk that a demand slowdown becomes a credit event.

insights.claim: Banks are offloading AI data-center exposure: ING put $500 million of data center loans up for sale, HSBC sold $300 million of Stargate-linked loans at a big discount, and Societe Generale is seeking buyers for $300 million of Oracle-related debt.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Discounted loan sales reveal private marks on AI infrastructure credit; watch secondary pricing of data-center debt.

insights.claim: CoreWeave bonds yield around 18%, deep junk territory, and CoreWeave has signed compute deals with VC-funded startups whose revenue could disappear, a dot-com-like vulnerability.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Neocloud cost of capital is a stress gauge for the AI build-out; counterparty risk on startup customers is underpriced.

insights.claim: Nvidia functions as the central bank of the AI build-out, financing neoclouds and startups from the bottom of the stack, so pressure on Nvidia stock reflects the whole complex being stress-tested.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Nvidia's equity and vendor-financing exposure make it the key node for contagion across AI credit.
insights.quote: Nvidia's been talked about as like the central bank of the AI build out

insights.claim: The AI sell-off resembles 2022 (Nasdaq -36% over 13 months) rather than the dot-com bust (-80% over 31 months) or 2008, implying a Nasdaq drawdown of roughly 30-40% versus about 20% so far.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: Base case leaves another 10-20 points of downside in tech but not a catastrophic collapse.

insights.claim: This is not a 2008-style credit crisis because AI leverage has only built for about 2.5 years versus seven years for the housing bubble, and unlike 2000, today's AI spenders are the strongest balance sheets with real revenue such as Anthropic's.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: Argues against positioning for systemic collapse; a cyclical bear in AI equities is more likely.

insights.claim: Like the railroad build-out, the AI infrastructure build-out can suffer bear-market-scale crashes and then resume; OpenAI and Anthropic have captured only about 3% of their addressable market, so the build-out may resume around late 2027 after a rough six months.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Long-term AI bulls may treat the next ~6 months as an accumulation window rather than a thesis break.

insights.claim: Market psychology is shifting in real time from correction (buy the dip) to bear market (sell any 10% pump).
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: In a bear regime, rallies become exits; adjust tactics from dip-buying to fading bounces.

insights.claim: AI with human assistance reportedly proved the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis, with the proof machine-checked the next day, raising the question of what other hard math AI can now solve.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: Rapid AI math capability is the root of the new crypto tail risk around cryptographic assumptions.

insights.claim: Scott Aaronson has heard rumors that one or both frontier labs are sitting on factoring in P, and Andrew Critch relayed rumors that Anthropic and OpenAI may have weakened RSA encryption; Bitcoin and Ethereum use ECDSA rather than RSA, but a break of one hard problem raises the question of whether ECDSA is next.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: Unconfirmed rumors are being priced as a tail risk into crypto; a lab announcement could be a major volatility event.
insights.quote: I've now heard many many rumors that one or both labs

insights.claim: If P equals NP, breaking cryptography would require only sufficiently smart algorithms rather than quantum computers, though Scott Aaronson still puts about 96% odds on P not equaling NP.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: Shifts the crypto security threat from a hardware timeline (quantum) to an unpredictable software/AI timeline.
insights.quote: Turns out you don't need quantum computers, you just need really smart algorithms.

insights.claim: P vs NP is not binary for crypto: a marginal or inscrutable result (like OpenAI only slightly breaking the exponential time hypothesis) would not practically break ECDSA, so investors should not assume a lab announcement kills crypto.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Avoid panic-selling on headline P=NP claims; the practical impact depends on how strong the result is.

insights.claim: Ethereum is accelerating its roadmap to replace ECDSA with hash-based cryptography rather than lattice-based schemes, which have more surface area for AI to attack.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: A credible post-quantum/post-AI roadmap could become a relative-value catalyst for ETH, which has been down only.
insights.quote: replacing things like ECDSA with hashes all the way down

insights.claim: AI-cryptography fears may be partly why non-Bitcoin store-of-value assets with more flexible upgrade paths, such as Zcash and Pearl, have been gaining ranking, while Bitcoin's constrained governance is overloaded by needing both quantum and AI-resistance upgrades.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: Adaptability of protocol governance could drive relative performance among store-of-value coins; Chris Berninsky flagged Bitcoin needs a credible roadmap.

insights.claim: The Sky token (formerly MKR) fell 30-40% in two weeks to its lowest price since around 2018 after it emerged that North Korea's Lazarus Group laundered USDC through Sky's price stability mechanism.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Protocol-level illicit-finance exposure can crater governance tokens and invite regulatory risk.

insights.claim: Sky founder Rune Christensen used Sky as a margin loan to himself, repaid $3 million but still owes $77 million, contributed to staked sUSD withdrawals being blocked, and is seeking to sell Sky to institutions to cover it.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Founder leverage on concentrated native tokens (as with Curve's founder in 2024) creates overhang and forced-selling risk.
insights.quote: this is on me. I got overconfident in Sky's strength.

insights.claim: Venice (VVV) crossed $200 million in annualized revenue, doubling from $100 million in about 100 days, and its token is trading near $27.50 versus a $34 all-time high, up 10-20% in a week during the bear market.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Fast-growing real revenue is one of the few sources of token relative strength in this bear.

insights.claim: Fidelity now lets customers trade DeFi tokens including UNI, Aave and Link, a major distribution milestone that went largely unnoticed in the bear market.
insights.speaker: Ryan Sean Adams
insights.so_what: Brokerage access builds pipes for retail/institutional demand that could amplify a future DeFi recovery.

insights.claim: The Senate is passing the Death Bets Act banning prediction contracts tied to death, terrorism and war; David Hoffman argues war markets carry real information value, unlike markets on named individuals' deaths.
insights.speaker: David Hoffman
insights.so_what: Regulatory scope on event contracts could limit some prediction-market categories.
